verifications.claim: NASA is set to launch Artemis II no earlier than April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'liftoff no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1'; R3: 'NASA is targeting Wednesday, April 1, at 6:24 p.m. ... from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B'; R6: 'At 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday ... from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the exact date, time, and location matching the claim.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed Moon mission since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'For the first time since 1972, NASA is sending humans back on a path toward the Moon'; R6: 'first people to launch toward the moon since the Apollo 17 mission in 1972'; R7: 'humanity's first flight to the moon since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in multiple sources confirm it as the first crewed mission since 1972.

verifications.claim: Four astronauts will conduct a 10-day around-the-moon test flight for Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'four astronauts ... on a 10-day mission'; R4: 'four astronauts ... on a 10-day mission'; R5: 'four astronauts ... on an approximately 10-day journey around the Moon'; R6: 'four astronauts ... 10-day journey that will take them looping around Earth and the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on number of astronauts, duration, and mission type in several sources.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of Artemis II is available via NASA+, YouTube, and Amazon Prime.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Full launch coverage begins at 12:50 p.m. on NASA+, Amazon Prime, and YouTube'; R11: 'NASA+, YouTube, and Amazon Prime'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly list these platforms for live coverage.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'NASA’s first crewed mission under the Artemis program, Artemis II will send ... on an approximately 10-day journey around the Moon'; R6: '10-day journey that will take them looping around Earth and the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Precise description of mission goal matches across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft around the Moon'; R2: 'Space Launch System rocket ... Orion spacecraft'; R5: 'SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II as first crewed test of SLS and Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and ... Jeremy Hansen'; R5: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA ... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed in multiple references.

verifications.claim: Primary launch window for Artemis II opens on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA is targeting Wednesday, April 1'; R5: 'no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1'; R6: 'At 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify April 1 as the target opening of the launch window.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch has an 80% chance of favorable weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'The weather forecast for launch day shows an 80% chance of favorable weather conditions'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote matches the exact percentage.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch weather monitoring is primarily for clouds and wind.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'primary concerns being cumulus clouds, ground winds, and solar weather'
verifications.reasoning: Source lists primary concerns as clouds and winds (plus solar, but primarily matches).

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will fly beyond the Moon, perform a U-turn, and return.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'They'll hurtle several thousand miles beyond the moon, hang a U-turn and then come straight back'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing of flying beyond Moon and U-turn in reference.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch is expected to be visible from parts of Florida and southern Georgia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Nearly all of Florida ... and those in southern Georgia, may be able to see Artemis II lift off'

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned as the first human landing in this program.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Artemis III ... low-Earth orbit'; R10: 'Artemis III mission no longer aims to send humans to moon ... NASA plans to put astronauts on the moon on the Artemis IV mission in 2028'
verifications.reasoning: References state Artemis III is now low-Earth orbit test, not first landing; first landing shifted to Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis III aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Artemis III, aims to conduct further technology demonstrations in low-Earth orbit'; R10: 'Artemis III mission no longer aims to send humans to moon'
verifications.reasoning: Direct contradiction; Artemis III no longer plans lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis III has potential adjustments in strategy and timing to ensure safety.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R10: 'radical changes to its delayed Artemis III mission ... new, more incremental approach ... to test flight and refine its technology ... adjustments in strategy and timing'
verifications.reasoning: Source describes changes and delays for safety and incremental approach.

verifications.claim: SpaceX is developing the Starship Human Landing System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA to return astronauts to the moon using its Starship rocket. The Artemis III mission will attempt to land a crew on the moon'; R9: 'Starship Human Landing System'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mentions of SpaceX developing Starship as HLS for NASA.

verifications.claim: SpaceX is targeting uncrewed lunar landing tests in 2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The company is targeting an uncrewed lunar landing in March 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement of uncrewed lunar landing target in 2027.
